mission: Make Buddy able to build, test, diagnose, repair, version, package and document DreamCo locally without requiring GitHub or internet access. GitHub is a synchronization and collaboration provider, not the runtime owner.
principles: same tests locally and in GitHub Actions
no cloud-only capability may be required for core Buddy operation
offline actions queue for later optional synchronization
human approval remains required for consequential external actions

local_equivalents.GitHub repository: local folder plus optional local git repository
local_equivalents.branches: local git branches or workspace snapshots
local_equivalents.commits: local git commits or signed change journal
local_equivalents.Actions: local task/test runner with logs, exit codes and artifacts
local_equivalents.pull requests: local change bundle with diff, tests, review checklist and approval state
local_equivalents.Pages: local static website build plus localhost file server
local_equivalents.releases: versioned local release bundles with manifest/checksum/changelog
local_equivalents.Dependabot: local dependency freshness report plus optional update recipes
local_equivalents.Agents: local Buddy worker roles with task files, tools and evidence
local_equivalents.Projects: local board/backlog JSON grouped by status/owner/priority
local_equivalents.GitHub sync: optional outbound adapter when network and permission are available

self_working_code_loop: detect changed files and affected tests
propose one or more bounded repair candidates
apply only locally safe deterministic repairs automatically
add regression fixture when a real defect is fixed
safe_automatic_repairs: regenerate derived files using canonical generators
truth_rule: Buddy can reproduce many repository-development and automation functions locally, but hosted GitHub services such as GitHub's global network, cloud runners, hosted pull-request UI, GitHub-specific security intelligence and organization controls remain GitHub services. Offline Buddy provides functional local equivalents where practical, not a claim of identical hosted infrastructure.
